title: Ýatla word entry
description: One vocabulary entry in the Ýatla content pipeline. Field names match the WORDS[] object shape already used in app-yatla.html (en, tm, ru, ipa, pos, def, ex, exTm, syn, coll, cefr, ox, stage).

en.description: The English headword, or a phrase the book teaches as a unit ("turn left", "Excuse me, where is the station").

tm.description: Turkmen translation. Latin script with Ý ý Ä ä Ň ň Ö ö Ü ü Ç ç Ş ş. No Cyrillic.

ipa.description: IPA transcription wrapped in slashes, e.g. "/həˈləʊ/" — the app prints w.ipa verbatim next to the headword.

pos.description: Part of speech, UPPERCASE — app-yatla.html prints w.pos verbatim. NUM = number, ORD = ordinal; both appear in the Beginner units on numbers.

def.description: English definition, learner-friendly and CEFR-matched. Lowercase start and no trailing full stop, matching the demo data.

exTm.description: Turkmen translation of the example sentence.

exRu.description: Optional Russian translation of the example sentence.

syn.description: Synonyms as a single comma-separated STRING (the app prints w.syn directly). Use "—" when there are none, as the demo data does.

coll.description: Collocations as a single comma-separated STRING. Use "—" when there are none.

ox.description: Word-list badge text, printed verbatim on the word detail card.

stage.description: Memory stage label. MUST be one of these five: app-yatla.html looks up STAGE_C[w.stage] for the chip colour and t(STAGE_K[w.stage]) for the label. Any other value renders background:undefined and the raw key.

books.description: Where this word is taught. `book` uses the app's BOOKS ids: beg, ele, pre, int, upp, adv, intp, advp (these drive the bk_* i18n keys). `unit` is the unit number; `lesson` is the English File lesson inside that unit (1A, 1B, 1C, 2A, ...) — English File teaches every unit as three lessons and the Vocabulary Bank maps onto those lessons, so a word belongs to a lesson, not just to a unit.

unit.description: The unit this book teaches the word in. Positive whole number; there is no ceiling, because not every book has twelve units.

lesson.description: Lesson inside the unit, e.g. 1A. The letter is A, B or C; the number must equal `unit`.

section.description: Which part of the lesson introduced the item (spec §8 content type). Derived from the source only when the source location is known; see `confidence`. Never guessed from topic similarity.

confidence.description: Extraction confidence (spec §14). high = explicitly listed, defined, glossed or drilled as target vocabulary; medium = strong contextual evidence the book intentionally introduces it; low = it merely occurs in a text. low items must never be auto-merged into the shipped word bank. Curated entries imported from the Vocabulary Bank and in-lesson VOCABULARY boxes are high by definition.

proofread.description: Set true only after a native TM/RU speaker has checked tm, ru and exTm. Validator reports the un-proofread count.

tags.description: Optional thematic tags used for lesson grouping.
